newsitem.title: USA: Texas hospital in IRS talks over tax-exempt bonds.
newsitem.headline: Texas hospital in IRS talks over tax-exempt bonds.

text.p: A Lubbock, Texas hospital says it is trying to settle a dispute with the Internal Revenue Service over the tax-exempt status of outstanding revenue bonds, according to notices obtained by Reuters.
Methodist Hospital said IRS last year threatened to revoke the hospital's tax-exempt status under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code.

At issue is the hospital's purchase of an air ambulance service and an interim office space lease, lawyers for the hospital said in notices filed with nationally recognized municipal securities information repositories.

The lawyers said that the hospital got a tentative green light from the federal government for a merger with a group called Sisters of St. Joseph of Orange. The only roadblock is the continuing talks with IRS over the hospital's 501(c)(3) status, they said.
"Representatives of the hospital and IRS are continuing to meet periodically to discuss the dispute," lawyers said.
The hospital says it offered to make a payment to the federal government to settle the issue and retain its 501(c)(3) status.
The bonds are Lubbock Health Facilities Development Corporation Hospital Revenue Bonds.
